The Type 49 racing installation is documented as a five-speed manual/Hewland family box. The Hewland DG300 manual identifies face-dog clutch rings and selector components. The Type 49 uses a driver-operated lever; the visible cockpit is consistent with the manual H-pattern installation. An H-pattern driver-shifted racing gearbox requires declutching to launch from rest. Hewland dog engagement is driven with clutchless running upshifts. Driver unloading of the dog ring is the documented mechanical technique. No electronic cut system is documented for the period manual installation. Manual blip is a downshift action. Automatic blip is a downshift action and no such system is documented. The dogbox permits authentic running downshifts without clutch operation when the driver matches revs. Throttle lift is modeled for upshift unloading. No downshift cut action is documented. Dog engagement requires manual rev matching on the downshift. The period installation has no documented automatic blip system. The inspected Lotus 49 cockpit image shows a continuous round conventional rim. No readout is carried on the wheel. No wheel-mounted shift lights are visible. The rim is closed and continuous. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/shift_pattern.
